subject: Preserve+Investigate: brief hold on deletion for live triage — FinAnalytics
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@finanalytics.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: support@finanalytics.com
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Strange tokenization regressions during batch run — need hold on deletion

Hi Kimberly,

We're in the middle of a high-priority reconciliation batch and saw repeated tokenization mismatches that only appear in a narrow time window on 2028-03-28 03:00-03:30 UTC. Our engineering lead suspects this is related to a KV-cache corruption in the traces we ship, and they asked whether Redwood can hold the associated request traces and kernel dumps for a short investigation.

Files we can share: kernel trace (kernel_trace_20280328.tar.gz) and a trimmed request set. We understand Redwood's retention defaults — we only need a time-limited preservation (48 hours) to triage and reproduce.

Can you confirm if this is possible and what approvals are required? We're on a tight reporting window for our audit.

Thanks,
Daniel Cho
Engineering Manager, FinAnalytics
---
Attachment: kernel_trace_20280328.tar.gz (application/gzip, 42MB stub)
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@finanalytics.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Strange tokenization regressions during batch run — need hold on deletion

Daniel —

Thanks for the heads up and for attaching the trace. We can typically grant a brief preservation window for debugging but need a documented scope, justification, and an internal owner to limit exposure. Please confirm:

- Exact time range of requests to preserve: 2028-03-28 03:00:00 - 03:35:00 UTC
- Artifact list: kernel_trace_20280328.tar.gz, trimmed-requests.json (you said you'd send)
- Desired hold duration: 48 hours
- Business justification: post-batch reconciliation impacting balances for several clients; audit due 2028-04-01

If that's correct, I'll kick off an internal approval and tag this as an exception tied to FinAnalytics. Ben, can you advise on the minimal-mitigation controls we should apply (access list, log audit) while this is preserved? Grace — FYI for audit trail.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: triage-checklist.pdf (application/pdf, 180KB stub)
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, daniel.cho@finanalytics.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Strange tokenization regressions during batch run — need hold on deletion

Kimberly / Daniel —

I can support the hold. Proposed controls:
- Preservation window: 48 hours as requested; we will auto-expire at 2028-03-31 09:47:00 -07:00 unless extended via this thread.
- Access: limit to Redwood SRE (ben.carter, infra-sre@redwood.ai) + FinAnalytics engineers (daniel.cho@finanalytics.com). No other internal teams.
- Auditing: enable elevated audit retention for these artifacts and export an access log snapshot to the FinAnalytics S3 share.
- Redaction: if PII appears in the traces we can redact request bodies on export; need Daniel to confirm acceptable redaction rules.

Daniel — please respond OK to the controls or suggest tighter constraints. Once you confirm, I'll mark the artifacts as preserved and generate the exception ticket (INF-4821).

-ben
Ben Carter
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@finanalytics.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Strange tokenization regressions during batch run — need hold on deletion

Ben —

OK to your proposed controls. A couple notes:
- Redaction: we prefer minimal redaction; please redact only account numbers (last 4 preserved) and session tokens. Leave request timestamps and tokenization context intact.
- Export: please push access logs to our S3 share at s3://finanalytics-redwood-exchange/traces/INF-4821/
- Extension: if triage requires more than 48 hours we'll request via the same thread with justification.

Thanks,
Daniel
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, daniel.cho@finanalytics.com
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Approval granted: short-term retention carveout (INF-4821)

All —

I reviewed the request and controls. Approving a 48-hour preservation window with the access and redaction constraints Ben proposed. I also require the following be captured in the exception ticket:
- Exact artifact checksums for trace verification
- Owner for the extension request (must be a FinAnalytics engineer)
- A named Redwood reviewer who will close the exception with a short post-mortem note.

Ben — please proceed to create the exception record and toggle the preservation flag. Kimberly — I'll need a short entry for the audit (one-paragraph summary) when this is complete.

-grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Compliance & Trust, Redwood Inference
